data.name: Check and explain
data.narration: The ruler measures the drawing. The scale tells us the actual distance. Both steps matter.
data.prompt: Describe the two steps you use to find a real-world distance.

data.name: Check the units
data.narration: Our converted number is larger because centimetres are smaller than metres. Label the answer centimetres.
data.prompt: What error happens if you write three hundred and twenty metres?
data.say: The units are essential. Three hundred and twenty metres would describe a very different beam.

time.label: Y7-050 · minutes to hours
time.rule: Divide the number of minutes by 60.
time.why: There are 60 minutes in one hour.

length.label: Y7-051 · metres to centimetres
length.why: Each metre contains one hundred centimetres.

area.label: Y7-051 · square centimetres to square millimetres
area.story: A tile has area 7.5 square centimetres.
area.why: One square centimetre covers a ten-by-ten grid of square millimetres.

volume.label: Y7-051 · litres to millilitres
volume.why: Each litre contains exactly one thousand millilitres.

euro.label: Y8-039 · pounds to euros
euro.rule: Multiply the pound amount by euros per pound.
euro.why: Each pound buys 1.25 euros at this stated example rate.
euro.explain: £80 × 1.25 = €100. This is a teaching rate, not a live quote.

speed.label: Y8-043 · km/h to m/s
speed.story: A vehicle travels at 72 kilometres per hour.
speed.rule: Multiply kilometres by 1,000 and hours by 3,600: divide the speed by 3.6.
speed.why: Both the distance and the time units must change.

density.label: Y9-024 · g/cm³ to kg/m³
density.story: The density is 1.5 grams per cubic centimetre.
density.rule: Change grams to kilograms AND cubic centimetres to cubic metres.

dollar.label: F18-09 / F6-12 · pounds to dollars
dollar.rule: Multiply pounds by the given dollars-per-pound rate.
dollar.why: One pound converts to 1.30 dollars in this illustrative exercise.
dollar.explain: £60 × 1.30 = $78. This is a teaching rate, not a live quote.

data.name: Check the angles
data.narration: Between each hour number is thirty degrees. Each minute is six degrees. At seven twenty-five the hour hand has moved from seven.
data.prompt: How could you find an angle between the hands?
data.say: Calculate each hand’s angle from twelve. Remember that the hour hand moves continuously, then compare.

p.label: Y7-050 · read an analogue clock
p.say: The long hand shows twenty-five minutes; the short hand has moved beyond seven.

data.name: Check the journey
data.narration: Forty-three minutes is the journey time. The answer is a duration, so it needs the unit minutes.
data.prompt: Why must we put minutes after forty-three?
data.say: Arrival time is a clock reading. Journey time is a duration: forty-three minutes.

bus.label: Y7 · City bus timetable
bus.context: A bus stops at four points across town.
bus.hint: Read down ONE service column, never mix two different buses.

school.label: Y7 · School arrival deadline
school.context: Find a bus that reaches school by 08:30.
school.hint: Compare the school arrival row with the deadline before choosing a departure.

rail.label: Y7 · Train connection at a junction
rail.context: Take train A to Junction, then connect to B or C.
rail.hint: A valid connection departs AFTER the first train arrives. The wait is departure minus arrival.

night.label: Y7 · Journey across midnight
night.context: These journeys cross midnight into the next day.
night.hint: Keep the next-day hour above 24:00 when subtracting, then display the time as a 24-hour clock reading.

midday.label: Y7 · Reading times across noon
midday.context: Track a bus from before noon into the afternoon.
midday.hint: 12:00 is noon. 13:00 is one in the afternoon.

data.name: Check the answer
data.narration: Three pounds and sixty-five pence plus six pounds and thirty-five pence makes ten pounds. The change is correct.
data.prompt: How can you prove the change is right?
data.say: Check by adding the price and the change. We land back on ten pounds.

till.label: Y7 · Correct change at the till
till.caption: Notebook and pencils
till.note: Pay £10.00 for a £6.35 purchase. Build the change from the coins.

cafe.label: Y7 · Notes, coins and mixed change
cafe.caption: Lunch at the café
cafe.note: A lunch costs £13.85. Pay with £20.00 and count back the change.

unit.label: Y7 · Best buy and unit prices
unit.caption: Compare yogurt multipacks
unit.note: Four yogurts cost £3.20; six cost £4.50. Compare the price PER yogurt.

budget.label: Y8 · Wages and spending budget
budget.caption: Weekly spending budget
budget.note: Your weekly wages are £98.00. Allow £25.65 for travel and food. What remains?

discount.label: Y8 · Sale price and change
discount.caption: Jacket sale
discount.note: A £20.00 jacket is reduced by 15%. Work out the new price, not the reduction.

cash.label: Y8 · Checkout subtraction
cash.caption: Sports equipment
cash.note: The total is £12.90 and the customer pays £20.00. Count back exactly.

data.name: Find money left and verify
data.narration: One hundred and six pounds, minus twenty-six pounds, leaves eighty pounds unallocated. Check by adding back the twenty-six pounds spent.
data.prompt: How can you check the remaining balance?
data.say: Add spending back to the remaining amount. Eighty pounds plus twenty-six pounds returns to net pay.

shift.label: First job · hourly wages
shift.note: Earn £9.50 for each of 12 hours. Subtract an example £8.00 deduction. Budget for transport and lunch.

overtime.label: Overtime · two pay rates
overtime.note: Work 16 hours at £11.50 and four overtime hours at £14.50. The 10% example deduction is not a real payroll rule.

payslip.label: Payslip · two deductions
payslip.note: Read each separate line on an illustrative payslip. Find take-home pay after both deductions.

weekly.label: Weekly budget · three expenses
weekly.note: Take-home pay funds everyday expenses. Only subtract spending after finding net pay.

savings.label: Savings plan · fixed amount
savings.note: Savings is an allocation of income. Include it when finding unallocated money.

percent.label: GCSE bridge · percentage deduction
percent.note: Seven percent of £268.80 is £18.816. Round to the nearest penny: £18.82. These deductions are fictional examples.

data.name: Calculate, compare and verify
data.narration: After five years, simple interest is fifty pounds. The compound gain, with annual penny rounding, is fifty-five pounds and twenty-seven pence.
data.prompt: What must you add to either interest amount to find the final savings balance?
data.say: Add the original two hundred pounds to the interest gained. Never confuse interest with final balance.

first.label: First savings · 5% for 5 years
first.desc: Start with £200 and earn five percent each year. Simple interest always uses the original £200.

holiday.label: Holiday fund · 8% for 3 years
holiday.desc: A £150 savings goal earns eight percent. Compare the same yearly add-on with interest on the growing balance.

regular.label: Junior saver · 3% for 5 years
regular.desc: Small annual percentages still build over time. Calculate three percent of the original £400.

smaller.label: Low rate · 2% for 4 years
smaller.desc: Two percent of £800 is £16. The simple-interest amount repeats every year.

gcse.label: GCSE extension · 6% for 5 years
gcse.desc: With compound interest, each new yearly percentage is calculated on the updated balance.

data.name: Generalise and transfer
data.narration: To find the top quantity, multiply the two bottom quantities. To find either bottom quantity, divide the top by the other bottom.
data.prompt: How would you find mass from density and volume?
data.say: The same structure works for density and pressure. Keep your units consistent.

speed.label: Speed · distance and time
speed.description: A train travels 150 kilometres in 2.5 hours. Speed is distance divided by time.
speed.hint: Start with distance travelled, then divide by the time in hours.

density.label: Density · mass and volume
density.description: A metal piece has mass 540 grams and volume 200 cubic centimetres. Density is mass per unit volume.
density.hint: Divide the mass by the volume, using matching units.

conversion.label: Convert rates · km/h to m/s
conversion.description: Convert 90 kilometres per hour to metres per second. The factor is 3.6 because 1 kilometre is 1000 metres and 1 hour is 3600 seconds.
conversion.hint: To change km/h to m/s, divide the number by 3.6.

multistep.label: Two-step speed · minutes to hours
multistep.description: A cyclist covers 36 kilometres in 45 minutes. Convert 45 minutes to 0.75 hours before dividing.
multistep.hint: Convert minutes into hours first; 45 minutes is 0.75 hours.

mass.label: Find mass · density × volume
mass.description: A liquid occupies 0.025 cubic metres and has density 800 kilograms per cubic metre. Multiply density by volume to obtain its mass.
mass.hint: When finding the top quantity, multiply the two bottom quantities.

pressure.label: Pressure · force and area
pressure.description: A force of 250 newtons acts over an area of 0.5 square metres. Pressure is force divided by area.
pressure.hint: Pressure in pascals equals newtons divided by square metres.

data.name: Compare and transfer
data.narration: The exact calculation gives a little more than our estimate. Estimation helps check whether a later exact result is reasonable.
data.prompt: What would make a predicted mass ten times too large?
data.say: Check the place value: one wrong zero can make a prediction ten times too large.

p.label: Deliveries · rounded mass
p.context: A school delivery has six full crates and a partially filled crate, equal to 6.1 full-crate loads. One full crate weighs 19.8 kg.
p.why: Round the mass to twenty kilograms and the number of crates to six. Multiply to make a quick prediction.
p.speech: A delivery contains about six crates at about twenty kilograms each. That is roughly one hundred and twenty kilograms.

data.name: Transfer to another accuracy
data.narration: The same idea works for decimals and for rounding to ten or one hundred. Change the rounding step, then halve it.
data.prompt: What changes if a measurement is given to the nearest tenth?
data.say: For tenths, the halfway margin is zero point zero five. The rule still works.

ruler.label: Length · nearest centimetre
ruler.context: A pencil is recorded as 12 cm to the nearest centimetre.

decimal.label: Length · nearest tenth
decimal.context: A ribbon is recorded as 3.7 m to the nearest tenth of a metre.

mass.label: Mass · nearest 10 grams
mass.context: A parcel has a recorded mass of 250 g to the nearest 10 g.

map.label: Distance · nearest 100 metres
map.context: A map records a distance of 1,200 m to the nearest 100 m.

rectangle.label: Area · two rounded lengths
rectangle.context: One side of a rectangle measures 8 m and the other measures 5 m, each to the nearest metre.

speed.label: Speed · limits from measurements
speed.context: A journey takes 2.0 h to the nearest 0.1 h; the distance is 120 km to the nearest kilometre.

challengeTasks.q: A board measures 16 cm to the nearest centimetre. Find its lower and upper bounds.
A rope is 5.3 m to the nearest tenth of a metre. Find its error interval.
A package is 470 g to the nearest 10 g. Give the bounds.
A road is measured as 1,800 m to the nearest 100 m. Give its error interval.
A garden length is 9 m, rounded to the nearest metre. Give the bounds of this length.
A journey time is 3.2 h to the nearest 0.1 h. Give the bounds of the time.

data.name: Transfer to area and volume
data.narration: For area, the length scale factor must be squared. For volume, it must be cubed. A squared or cubed unit changes more quickly than a length.
data.prompt: Why does a square metre contain ten thousand square centimetres?
data.say: Remember: length times one hundred, area times ten thousand, volume times one million.

desk.label: Desk length · m to cm
desk.title: Measuring a desk
desk.story: A long studio desk measures 2.6 metres. How many centimetres is that?
desk.tip: One metre contains one hundred centimetres. Multiply the metres by one hundred.

trail.label: Walking route · km to m
trail.title: Walking-route sign
trail.story: A sign gives a walking distance of 1.75 kilometres. Express the distance in metres.
trail.tip: One kilometre contains one thousand metres.

floor.label: Room floor · m² to cm²
floor.title: Tiling the classroom
floor.story: A floor section covers 2.4 square metres. How many square centimetres is that?
floor.tip: A square metre is one hundred centimetres by one hundred centimetres, so there are ten thousand square centimetres.

poster.label: Poster area · cm² to m²
poster.title: Designing a poster wall
poster.story: A poster design occupies 6,500 square centimetres. Express the area in square metres.
poster.tip: To change square centimetres into square metres, divide by ten thousand.

crate.label: Storage box · m³ to cm³
crate.title: Packing a storage box
crate.story: A storage crate has a volume of 0.035 cubic metres. Express this in cubic centimetres.
crate.tip: A cubic metre contains one hundred by one hundred by one hundred cubic centimetres: one million.

water.label: Drinks dispenser · L to mL
water.title: Filling a drinks dispenser
water.story: A drinks dispenser contains 1.8 litres of water. How many millilitres is that?
water.tip: One litre equals one thousand millilitres.

challengeTasks.story: A wooden shelf is 3.7 m long. Give the length in cm.
A cycle path is 2.45 km long. Give its length in m.
A floor mat covers 1.8 m². Give its area in cm².
An exhibition panel covers 45,000 cm². Give its area in m².
A case encloses 0.024 m³. Give its volume in cm³.
A jug holds 2.75 L. Give its capacity in mL.
